subject: Geo-locking requirements, log retention, and cross-region backups — next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@vitahealth.co>, VitaHealth Legal <legal@vitahealth.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: geo residency & retention items from today's call

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a clear list of asks and next steps on the data residency / retention fronts. Please confirm or correct the bold items below and attach any formal policy excerpts we should reference.

High-level customer constraints (from call):
- Production data must be anchored in the EU (primary region preference).
- Backups: you said backups should also remain in the EU unless specifically approved.
- PII classification and retention: there are multiple classes (PHI-like health identifiers + customer metadata) — need exact retention windows per class.
- Audit logs & access logs: legal requires logs for incident investigation and potential audits. Please confirm retention horizon and whether aggregated logs are acceptable for some use cases.
- Cross-region failover: you flagged a potential requirement for a short-duration failover to a US warm-standby only under an outage; this needs strict controls (CMK, access controls, and post-failover data handling).

Specific asks (we can take these into the technical deep-dive):
1) Confirm canonical region binding: which AWS/Azure region(s) do you require as primary for production and for backups? (exact cloud region strings help: e.g., eu-west-1)
2) Per-data-class retention: production payload (PII) retention period, event logs retention, audit logs retention, and backups snapshot retention.
3) Cross-region failover policy: allowed? allowed duration? required encryption/KMS posture? required notification/approval flows?
4) Acceptable pseudonymization/anonymization approaches vs. deletion for older records.
5) Any contractual redlines on audit log access (e.g., only aggregated logs to third parties, Redwood engineers require approved SSO + Just-In-Time access, etc.)

I've attached a short VH security checklist (please fill) and a copy of the retention doc you promised. Once we have the confirmed windows and failover constraints, Ben and Karthik will scope recommended configuration + impact on latency/cost.

Attachments: VH-Security-Checklist.xlsx (stub), VitaHealth_Retention_Policy_v1.pdf (stub)

Thanks — I will tentatively schedule a 60-minute technical session for next week with Ben & Karthik; happy to move it once we see your timings.

Best,
Monica Patel

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@vitahealth.co>

Cc: VitaHealth Legal <legal@vitahealth.co>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 20:41:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up: geo residency & retention items from today's call

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear recap. I asked our security and legal teams to confirm specifics; attaching the retention policy and a completed security checklist for your reference. Quick answers inline below — we'll follow up with any formal redlines from Legal.

Inline responses:
- Canonical region binding: Production and backups must be in the EU (preferred eu-west-1).
- Backups: daily snapshots retained for 365 days; backups must be stored in EU-only storage.
- PII retention: two tiers — (1) Identifiers (name, email, national id): retain up to 2 years post-last-activity; (2) Transactional event payloads (operational logs referencing users): retain up to 90 days unless flagged for investigation.
- Audit logs & access logs: retain for 3 years; must be tamper-evident and include IAM principals + IP. Aggregated metrics ok for analytics, but raw access logs must be available on request to Legal.
- Cross-region failover: allowed for up to 48 hours only under declared outage. Conditions: (a) customer-managed KMS (CMK) must be in place; (b) access controls must be reapplied post-failback and an incident report provided; (c) Legal approval required before failover if the event is not a total region outage.

Notes from Legal: they will send formal redlines if any; expect those within 3 business days.

Attaching: VitaHealth_Retention_Policy_v1.pdf (stub), VH-Security-Checklist.xlsx (stub)

Thanks,
Samantha Liu
Head of Platform Ops | VitaHealth
samantha.liu@vitahealth.co

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2029 01:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: geo residency & retention items from today's call

On Mon, Jul 22, 2029 at 8:41 PM Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@vitahealth.co> wrote:
> Inline responses:
> - Canonical region binding: Production and backups must be in the EU (preferred eu-west-1).
> - Backups: daily snapshots retained for 365 days; backups must be stored in EU-only storage.
> - PII retention: two tiers — identifiers 2 years; transactional payloads 90 days.
> - Audit logs & access logs: retain for 3 years; tamper-evident.
> - Cross-region failover: allowed up to 48 hours with CMK and Legal approval.

Thanks — quick technical read: all of these are implementable on Redwood Dedicated/Private and hosted with controls. Notes and open items for scoping: 
1) Region pinning: we can pin production model serving to eu-west-1 and configure backups to the same region. For hosted accounts we use region affinity; for Dedicated we can allocate capacity in that region.
2) Backups + snapshots: daily snapshot + 365d retention is straightforward; need to confirm snapshot format (encrypted object store vs. full VM image) — this affects restore time.
3) Cross-region failover: we support configurable warm-standby in another region, and we can limit automated failover duration (we'll implement a 48-hour timer and an alerting/approval gate). Important: warm-standby must not continuously replicate decrypted payloads across borders — we can replicate encrypted snapshots only and require rehydration in EU on failback unless customer permits temporary decrypted caching in US under CMK with strict access logs.
4) KMS / CMK: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) in both hosted and private modes. Need to confirm whether VitaHealth will provide a key in eu-west-1 or expect Redwood to provision a dedicated CMK with customer access.
5) Audit logs: we can provide tamper-evident logs via append-only storage + signed digests. We need to know the specific fields Legal wants and whether Redwood will be allowed to export those logs to VitaHealth's log retention target.

Can we action the following prior to the deep-dive?
- Samantha/VH: confirm CMK approach (customer-provided or Redwood-hosted but customer-controlled).
- VH Legal: any absolute prohibition on replicated encrypted snapshots crossing to US during failover?
- Monica: I will draft an ops configuration that lists the trade-offs (restore RTO, cost delta for warm-standby, and key management flow).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
